analysis.title: Models Come And Go, Powered Compute Is Forever: Goldman Says Hyperscalers Deserve Their Premium
key_insights: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky argues the durable moat in AI is owned, powered compute, not frontier models. Model leadership can change quarterly, while ownership of powered compute is a much more durable advantage.

Compute is scarce, and its owners benefit most. Part of the scarcity is market doubt about the Street's ability to bring power and data center capacity online, which is driving a de-rating in the data center supply chain.
Hyperscalers have invested most aggressively in scarce compute and can command premium economics. Privorotsky says the market is right to reward them.
The model leaderboard is unsettled. Google is reportedly testing a model called Carbon, potentially competitive with Opus 5.5, and OpenAI and Anthropic have unreleased models.

A Polymarket snapshot in the note shows Anthropic's lead in the 'best model at end-2026' market collapsing in late September while Google surged. On Oct 12 the market priced Google at 43%, Anthropic 42%, OpenAI 9%, Meta 3% and xAI 2%, on $2.4MM of volume.

The OpenAI ARR scare on Oct 8 (FT: annualized revenue near $50BN, about $20BN below the circulating figure) is described by Privorotsky as largely an accounting definition issue, gross versus net booking of partner/cloud sales.
Privorotsky says the market reaction to the OpenAI headline suggests more length and increasing sensitivity in crowded AI positioning.
Goldman's September bar for continued hyperscaler spending is that token demand growth must outpace declining token prices. Open-source models have contributed to falling token prices.

Power is the binding constraint. Prior reporting cited: about 5GW of ~16GW planned US data center capacity under construction, Wood Mackenzie finding over two-thirds of requested power will not materialize, ERCOT interconnection requests at 474GW against 91GW peak Texas demand.
Goldman's commodity team expects behind-the-meter generation to power 25% of data centers by 2030, from effectively 0% in 2025.

Goldman TMT's Peter Callahan cites a still durable bull case of compute demand outstripping supply, supporting confidence in 2027+ capex. Dell management told Goldman that supply remains the primary gating factor to AI infrastructure growth.
Goldman Prime data show US hedge funds rotated into Industrials and out of Info Tech, a reversal of the September trend, with Tech selling most pronounced Thursday on the OpenAI headline.

Info Tech was the most net sold US sector this week at -1.0 standard deviations after being the most bought in 4 of the prior 5 weeks. Fundamental L/S net leverage is 52.9%, 6th percentile on a 1-year lookback.

ASML reports Wednesday and TSMC Thursday. ASML is reportedly raising spare parts prices 10%. TSMC had its biggest 4-day pullback since late July, down about 7% Tuesday to Friday, with focus on the 2027+ capex outlook.

market_movers.rationale: TSMC fell about 7% Tue-Fri, its biggest 4-day pullback since late July, with investors focused on 2027+ capex ahead of Thursday earnings.
ASML reports Wednesday and is reportedly raising spare parts prices 10%, which Privorotsky reads as inconsistent with collapsing demand.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were heavy net sellers of Info Tech this week, but the note says there is still a ton of capacity to add AI exposure and the compute scarcity thesis is intact.
Hedge funds rotated into Industrials, reversing the September trend.

earnings_insights: ASML reports Wednesday (Oct 14) and TSMC Thursday (Oct 15) before the open. No consensus figures are given in the note.
Goldman analysts' 2027E/2028E TSMC capex estimates are cited in the note, but the figures are garbled in the extracted text and cannot be read reliably.
Dell management told Goldman's Katherine Murphy that supply remains the primary gating factor to AI infrastructure growth.
risk_factors: Token demand may fail to outpace falling token prices, which would undermine hyperscaler investment spending.
Crowded positioning in AI names is sensitive to headlines such as the OpenAI ARR report.
Power and data center build delays could continue to pressure the data center supply chain.
TSMC 2027+ capex guidance on Thursday and ASML results Wednesday are near-term tests.

tension_points.theme: AI model moat vs compute moat
tension_points.bull_case: Owners of powered compute have a durable advantage and hyperscalers deserve premium economics, since model leadership changes quarterly.
tension_points.bear_case: Token prices are falling as open-source models compete, and token demand may not outpace them, which would weaken the case for continued hyperscaler capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Token demand growth failing to outpace declining token prices, per Goldman's September bar for continued spending.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge fund books have shrunk, so there is still a ton of capacity to add AI exposure.
tension_points.bear_case: The sharp reaction to the OpenAI ARR headline suggests crowded length and increasing sensitivity in AI positioning.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ASML results Wednesday and TSMC's capex guide Thursday are the near-term tests.
